# Jaylen Brown TRADED | Kessler To LA | NBA Free Agency Day 2

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-07-02, 42:39. https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY

## Summary

Josh Lloyd covers day 2 of NBA free agency, focusing on three trades and about 20 signings. The biggest move sends Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia for Paul George. Lloyd says Brown's fantasy value drops because his usage will fall next to Maxey and Embiid, and George's value rises with a bigger role in Boston. Utah trades Walker Kessler to the Lakers. That opens a fantasy path for Jusuf Nurkic if he starts, and Lloyd warns that Kessler will be overdrafted as a three-category player. He also goes through signings like John Collins to Detroit, Norman Powell to Chicago, Tobias Harris to San Antonio and the Lakers' depth moves, and calls most of them low fantasy impact or harmful to the players already there.

## Rules and methods

- [9:40](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=580) A high-usage scorer who moves next to other high-usage, ball-dominant players will see his usage and on-ball role shrink, which lowers his value.
  > "So even if Embiid is out, Brown gets usage up, but he doesn't get on-ballness up."
- [18:03](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1083) Players who are elite in only three categories (blocks, FG%, rebounds) get overdrafted in category leagues. Don't take them as early as round three.
  > "will be somebody in fantasy drafts I think in category leagues not points leagues in category leagues that will take Kessler"
- [22:14](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1334) A bench player who gets about 27 minutes a night is enough to be a later-round fantasy flyer.
  > "Cuz if he's a 27-minute a night sixth man, then we're in. Like that's that's enough."
- [28:15](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1695) A scorer who only gives points and threes needs high usage (around 28) and about 40% three-point shooting to be fantasy relevant.
  > "he needs to be a 40% three-point shooter and getting 28 usage to be fantasy relevant."
- [39:00](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=2340) When a team has too many players at the same positions, the minutes get spread thin and fewer players are draftable. Project the rotation before you reach for anyone.
  > "But, it's just extra depth that does mean that to me I I have to do it. I have to project it out."
- [30:53](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1853) Watch backup center battles behind injury-prone starters, because whoever gets those starts has fantasy value.
  > "Cuz whoever starts would be interesting to us from a fantasy point of view."
